name: July 2023 Yamuna Flood & Water Supply Cascade Disaster
description: Evidence-backed historical replay of the historic July 2023 Yamuna River flood in Delhi. River level thresholds are verified from CWC hydrometric data at Old Railway Bridge; WTP inundations and Sushruta Trauma Centre evacuation are sourced from NIDM/CWC reports.

primarySources.title: Delhi Floods - 2023: A Case Study (Central Water Commission, Jan 2025)
primarySources.citation: Pages 6, 9 (Old Railway Bridge HFL 208.66m, Hathnikund 3.59L cusecs)

primarySources.title: Impact of Inundation along River Yamuna in Delhi (NIDM, 2025)
primarySources.citation: Pages 77, 89, 93 (Wazirabad, Chandrawal, Okhla shutdowns; Sushruta evacuation)

nodes.assumption: Inundated and shut down on 13 July 2023 due to pump house submergence (NIDM Yamuna Report p.77).

nodes.assumption: Inundated and shut down on 13 July 2023 due to pump house submergence (NIDM Yamuna Report p.77).

nodes.name: Okhla Water Treatment Plant
nodes.assumption: Inundated and shut down on 13 July 2023 due to river flooding (NIDM Yamuna Report p.77).

nodes.name: Central Delhi Water Distribution Zone

nodes.name: Lok Nayak Hospital (LNJP / Delhi Gate)
nodes.assumption: Major referral center; received evacuated patients and emergency water tankers (NIDM Report p.77, p.89).

edges.assumption: Overbank floodwaters reach Wazirabad raw intake pump house (CWC/NIDM flood chronology).
Direct floodwater overtopping along Metcalf Road riverbank (NIDM Report p.77).
River backflow reaches Chandrawal pump station (NIDM Report p.77).
Plant shutdown causes immediate pressure loss in North zone mains.
Plant shutdown causes pressure loss in Central zone distribution network.
Municipal feeder connection to Civil Lines hospital.
Municipal feeder connection to LNJP hospital complex.

chronology.headline: Hathnikund Barrage releases peak monsoon discharge of 3.59 Lakh cusecs
chronology.description: Following extreme precipitation across the upper Yamuna catchment, Hathnikund Barrage released its peak monsoon flood discharge of 3.59 Lakh cusecs (10,165 cumecs) into the downstream Yamuna. CWC estimates flood travel time of 2.0 to 2.5 days to reach the Delhi NCT reach.
chronology.sourceLocator: CWC Delhi Floods 2023 Case Study, Section 2.1, Page 9

chronology.headline: Yamuna water level crosses official Warning Level (204.50 m) at Old Railway Bridge
chronology.description: The Old Railway Bridge CWC hydrometric station recorded river levels rising past the official warning threshold of 204.50 m, triggering initial municipal flood alerts.
chronology.sourceLocator: CWC Delhi Floods 2023 Case Study, Section 1, Page 6

chronology.headline: Yamuna crosses official Danger Level (205.33 m); low-lying evacuation initiated
chronology.description: River level breached the Danger Level of 205.33 m. Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) directed evacuation of floodplains across North, Central, and East Delhi districts.
chronology.sourceLocator: CWC Delhi Floods 2023 Case Study, Section 1, Page 6

chronology.headline: Yamuna level breaches 45-year-old Highest Flood Level (207.49 m)
chronology.description: At 13:00 hrs on 12 July 2023, the Yamuna River level at the Old Railway Bridge surpassed its previous Highest Flood Level of 207.49 m (set on 6 September 1978), reaching unprecedented flood heights.
chronology.sourceLocator: CWC Delhi Floods 2023 Case Study, Section 2.1, Page 9

chronology.locationName: Wazirabad, Chandrawal, and Okhla Water Treatment Plants
chronology.headline: Three major WTPs forced to shut down due to pump house inundation (-245 MGD capacity cut)
chronology.description: Raging Yamuna waters submerged intake pumps and raw water infrastructure at Wazirabad, Chandrawal, and Okhla WTPs, forcing complete plant shutdowns. Production at Sonia Vihar WTP was reduced by 25%. Drinking water supply rationalization declared across North, Central, and South Delhi.
chronology.sourceLocator: NIDM Yamuna Urban Flood Report, Section 5, Page 77 & 89

chronology.headline: Floodwaters inundate Sushruta Trauma Centre; emergency evacuation of patients initiated
chronology.description: River water overflowed into the premises of Delhi Government's Sushruta Trauma Centre at Metcalf Road, Civil Lines. Patients were evacuated and relocated to Lok Nayak (LNJP) Hospital and neighboring centers. Access to St. Stephen's Hospital was severely constrained.
chronology.sourceLocator: NIDM Yamuna Urban Flood Report, Section 5, Page 77

chronology.headline: Yamuna hits all-time peak crest of 208.66 m; Ring Road and Yamuna Bazar inundated under 8-10 ft
chronology.description: At 18:00 hrs on 13 July 2023, the Yamuna River reached its historic all-time crest of 208.66 m. River embankments overtopped between Wazirabad and Okhla. Yamuna Bazar, Nigambodh Ghat, Monastery Market, and Ring Road submerged under up to 10 feet of water.
chronology.sourceLocator: CWC Delhi Floods 2023 Case Study, Section 2.1, Page 9

chronology.headline: 26,401 citizens evacuated to relief camps; water tanker convoys mobilized for hospitals
chronology.description: Government of NCT of Delhi reported 26,401 evacuated citizens sheltered across camps and pucca school buildings. Emergency water tankers and health inspection teams mobilized to support critical facilities.
chronology.sourceLocator: NIDM Yamuna Urban Flood Report, Chapter 7, Page 93
